papers.title: Behavioral Public Economics
note: The chapter that draws the border around the field. Its organizing problem is what happens to welfare analysis once you admit that people make mistakes: revealed preference stops being a reliable statement about what is good for someone, so the planner needs a different object to maximize and a defensible way to recover it.

It works through corrective taxation, nudges and defaults, present bias, social insurance, household finance, and behavioral IO — which is also why it became the ontology backbone for the behavioral-econ-map on the other side of this page.
Replace this note with your own — it is a summary, not yet a reading.
